claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure containing dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Coarse internal phase boundaries in the untreated alloy are sites for dislocation pile-ups.
Dislocation pile-ups at coarse internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcrack initiation, and brittle failure.
The proposed intervention is cryogenic rolling followed by controlled annealing.
The annealing conditions should be tuned to produce partial recrystallization.
The intervention is applicable when tensile performance is evaluated at room temperature.
Cryo-rolling and annealing form a refined nano-lamellar hierarchical microstructure.
The processed FCC regions contain ultrafine grains.
The intervention reduces the coarseness of the B2 phase.
The refined hierarchical microstructure redistributes strain more uniformly.
Cryogenic rolling introduces dislocations under low-temperature conditions, and subsequent annealing produces controlled recovery and recrystallization.
Microstructural refinement reduces effective internal-boundary spacing and limits dislocation pile-ups.
Limiting dislocation pile-ups lowers local stress concentrations and suppresses microcracking and catastrophic failure.
Cryo-rolling followed by annealing simultaneously increases yield strength and tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy should attain a yield strength similar to or greater than approximately 1437 MPa.
The treated alloy should attain elongation to failure near or above 14%.

The intervention may apply broadly to eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies, although efficacy depends on chemistry, starting microstructure, rolling strain, cryogenic temperature, and annealing schedule.
